milestone: Fit passages to existing terrain and lower tunnel crowns
changes: Generate and validate the complete world before considering optional mountain crossings. Remove dedicated peak placement, region reservation and route-shaped raised foundations.
Filter directional WFC sockets by existing dry support, elevated road protection and reachable approaches. Failed candidates restore the completed world. No suitable crossing is a valid result.
Fit shallow surface bypasses to existing ground; preserve original landform, surface elevation, road, base and lake metadata.
Lower all eight mountain crowns from 3.6–6.8 to 3–5 quarter floors and deep-cave crowns from 4–5.5 to 3.3–4.5. Keep widths and physical clearance validation.
Preserve grass/soil on unchanged path surfaces and retain props outside the actual near-surface excavation footprint.

verified: Lower openings in existing hillsides; bypass retains surface materials with guides hidden.
Moving mountain scout triggers Auto cutaway, remains visible and can be paused inside. Same-camera Off/Auto comparison preserves surrounding cast shadows.
Deep-tunnel reveal, horizontal section, entrance ramp, isolated network with and without ceilings, and shared tile-boundary continuation.
No-crossing worlds retain the primary underground network and explain disabled mountain-tour controls.
Isolation changes neither the world hash nor the active route; no warning/error console entries.
browser_review.visibility_followup: The local geometry-review tab had cutaway set to Off. Restored Auto and verified the moving scout. Visibility and shadow shader code is unchanged from the prior shadow fix.

limits: Regional routes still use a cardinal WFC cycle grammar; this is not a geological cave or erosion simulation.
The existing base-road and landform planners retain their behavior. This pass does not redesign all base hills or roads.
Land remains 64 by 64 cells within the 96 by 96 ocean. Map expansion and general terrain-aware road search are future work.
Eighteen of 32 sampled worlds accepted optional crossings; this is a cohort observation, not a guaranteed frequency.
Terrain metadata invariance concerns the optional passage stage; excavation intentionally subtracts rock from the composed solid.
